rows.grounds: introduces the topic of the spatial path
refers to the procedure being described
grounds the teaching in scriptural authority

items.question: How is the path of space taught in the Shaiva scriptures?
premises: The path of space is now being explained.
It is taught through contraction and expansion.
This method is found in the Shaiva scriptures.
items.inference: The spatial path is presented scripturally by means of contraction and expansion.
items.plain_english: Now the path of space is also taught, through contraction and expansion, according to the method seen in the Shaiva scriptures.

rows.grounds: links the two paths to form and its diversity

items.question: What is the relationship between the path of time and the path of space?
premises: The path of time, consisting of the Lord's power of action, has already been examined.
The path of space arises in relation to the variety of forms.
The path of space is now being defined.
items.inference: After explaining the temporal path rooted in action, the text turns to the spatial path rooted in the diversity of forms.
uncertainties: The compound mūrtivaicitryajastajjo is compressed and may allow slightly different readings.
items.plain_english: The path of time, made of the Lord's power of action, has already been examined; now the path of space, connected with the variety of forms, is being defined.

rows.grounds: qualifies the path as a whole
describes lack of grounding in consciousness

items.question: Where is the entire path ultimately established?
premises: The entire path is established in consciousness alone.
Nothing can truly rest outside that consciousness.
What does not rest in consciousness is like a sky-flower.
items.inference: The whole spatial path has no reality apart from its grounding in consciousness.
items.plain_english: This entire path is established in consciousness alone; whatever does not rest there is as unreal as a flower in the sky.

rows.grounds: states the external placement of the path

items.question: Through what levels does the path of space become situated in the body?
premises: The path is manifested through consciousness.
It appears in subtle and inner loci such as void, intellect, vital airs, and channel-circles.
Its situation is also found in the outer body.
items.inference: The spatial path unfolds from consciousness through inner yogic levels into the outer body.
items.plain_english: Created through the door of consciousness, the path is situated in the void, in the intellect, in the vital airs, in the circles of channels, and also in the outer body.

rows.grounds: refers to the path as described
gives the reason for defining it

items.question: Why should the yogi carefully contemplate the structure of the path?
premises: The path must be properly defined in its procedural order.
A yogi can continually attend to that order.
Such contemplation leads quickly to the state of Bhairava.
items.inference: Contemplating the ordered structure of the path is a direct means for the yogi to attain Bhairava-hood.
items.plain_english: This path should be defined in this way, because by continually attending to its proper sequence the yogi can quickly attain the state of Bhairava.

items.question: What happens when awareness pervades all things through the desire to know them?
premises: A mere desire to see can become a mode of pervasion.
When one abides pervading all things, nothing further needs to be explained.
This teaching is stated in the Spanda scripture.
items.inference: Direct pervading awareness makes elaborate explanation unnecessary.
items.plain_english: When, by the mere desire to see, one abides pervading all things, what more needs to be said? So it is taught in the Spanda scripture.

rows.grounds: names the first locus of dissolution
names the next locus of dissolution

items.question: How should the yogi dissolve the entire path in contemplative practice?
premises: The entire path must first be known.
It should be dissolved into its governing lords.
Those lords should then be melted in sequence into body, breath, and mind.
items.inference: Contemplative mastery of the path proceeds by sequential dissolution from its rulers into the practitioner's inner system.
items.plain_english: Having known the entire path, one should dissolve it into its lords, and then, as before, melt them in sequence into the circle of body, breath, and mind.

rows.grounds: refers to everything dissolved so far
names the final locus of dissolution

items.question: What is the final result of dissolving everything into one's own consciousness?
premises: All that has been dissolved is finally absorbed into one's own consciousness.
That consciousness is full and self-sufficient.
When contemplated, it destroys the ocean of samsara.
items.inference: Contemplation of plenary consciousness culminates in the dissolution of samsara.
items.plain_english: All of that should be dissolved into one's own consciousness; when contemplated, that consciousness, full in its own nature, becomes the fire that dissolves the ocean of worldly existence.

rows.grounds: marks the lower limit of Vishnu's domain
marks the upper limit of Vishnu's domain

items.question: Which lords govern the lower ranges of the path according to the Mahikshottara?
premises: The Mahikshottara teaches the lords of the path.
Brahma governs from Ananta up to Pradhana.
Vishnu governs from Purusha up to Kala.
items.inference: The lower ranges of the path are apportioned among specific cosmic lords.
items.plain_english: In the revered Mahikshottara, the teacher declared these lords of the path: Brahma rules from Ananta up to Pradhana, and Vishnu from Purusha up to Kala.

rows.grounds: states Shiva's relation to the lower ranges
names the supreme beyond even that

items.question: How are the higher lords and the supreme principle arranged above the lower ranges?
premises: Rudra governs in the knot and Isha governs in Maya up to Sadakhya.
The unsupported Shiva pervades those domains.
Beyond that pervader is the supreme who pervades even him.
items.inference: The hierarchy culminates in a supreme principle that transcends and pervades all lower lords.
items.plain_english: Rudra rules in the knot, and Isha in Maya up to the range of Sadakhya; above them is the unsupported Shiva who pervades all that, and beyond him is the supreme who pervades even that.

rows.grounds: qualifies the kind of knowledge denied

items.question: What kind of knowledge is affirmed in the Svacchanda teaching about attaining Shiva-hood?
premises: One may understand oneself as having attained Shiva-hood.
This understanding is doctrinally defined.
It is not mere procedural knowledge.
items.inference: The realization of Shiva-hood is presented as more than technical or ritual procedure.
items.plain_english: Thus, understanding oneself as having attained Shiva-hood, it was defined in the Svacchanda teaching that this is not knowledge limited to mere procedure.

rows.grounds: identifies the content of that awareness
defines memory in terms of differentiation

items.question: How does the Trishiras teaching analyze awareness and memory?
premises: Awareness is conceived as root, middle, and tip.
This awareness unfolds as the thirty-six principles.
Memory is described as the construction of difference.
items.inference: The Trishiras teaching maps differentiated experience onto a threefold structure of awareness.
items.plain_english: In the Trishiras teaching, awareness is conceived as root, middle, and tip, unfolding as the thirty-six principles, while memory is the construction of difference.

items.question: What characterizes the root level of awareness in this teaching?
premises: The root of awareness is an 'I am' state with unobstructed distinction.
It contains the state of all principles.
In one's own self it remains undivided.
items.inference: The root level holds all principles together in a unified self-awareness.
items.plain_english: The root of awareness is the 'I am' state with unobstructed distinction; it is the state of all principles, present in one's own self without division.

items.question: How is the middle level of awareness distinguished from the root?
premises: The middle of awareness shows some relation of support and supported.
It arises through differentiation among the principles.
It is marked by each nature standing in its own form.
items.inference: The middle level is where unified awareness begins to appear as structured differentiation.
items.plain_english: The middle of awareness is marked by a certain relation of support and supported, arising through the differentiation of the principles and the standing of each in its own nature.

items.question: What defines the highest or tip level of awareness?
premises: The tip of awareness is clear, waveless, and full of vast bliss.
It brings beings, states, and bodies into oneness with consciousness.
It represents a unifying culmination of awareness.
items.inference: The highest level of awareness is a blissful, still unification of all differentiated experience in consciousness.
items.plain_english: The tip of awareness is clear, waveless, and full of vast bliss; it brings beings, states, bodies, and the rest into oneness with consciousness.

rows.grounds: describes the path as adorned by all principles

items.question: How is the supreme reality described in relation to the thirty-six principles?
premises: Unbroken consciousness is identified as Bhairava, the supreme Lord.
The Deviyayamala teaches this view.
The path is described as beautiful with the thirty-six principles.
items.inference: The supreme Bhairava is unbroken consciousness that encompasses the full system of thirty-six principles.
uncertainties: The exact title form śrīdevyāyāmale is transmitted in a compressed form.
items.plain_english: Unbroken consciousness is Bhairava, the supreme Lord; and in the revered Deviyayamala it is said that the path is beautiful with the thirty-six principles.

rows.grounds: describes the practice and its speed

items.question: What is the effect of meditating on the sixfold path, given the Lord's non-dual nature?
premises: Meditating on the sixfold path can make one immediately Shiva-like.
The Lord is not different from consciousness.
This raises a question about how spatial distinctions apply to such a Lord.
items.inference: Meditation on the sixfold path leads to identity with Shiva, even though Shiva transcends real spatial division.
items.plain_english: By meditating on the sixfold path one can immediately become of the nature of Shiva, even though that Lord is not different from consciousness.

items.question: If the full Lord has no real divisions, why speak of above, middle, and end?
premises: The full Lord has no real arrangement of above, beginning, middle, or end.
Teaching still requires communicable distinctions.
Such distinctions serve both students and teachers.
items.inference: Spatial divisions are pedagogical constructs, not ultimate realities in the full Lord.
items.plain_english: For the full Lord there is no real arrangement of above, beginning, middle, or end; nevertheless, such distinctions are used for the sake of those who must understand and for the one who teaches.

items.question: Why is the earthly principle treated as the lowest or innermost level?
premises: Conceptions like middle and so on arise according to one's own nature.
They are limited by the knower's conceptual framework.
Within that framework, the earthly principle is known as the lowest.
items.inference: The placement of the earthly principle is a function of cognitive convention, not of ultimate reality.
items.plain_english: Conceptions such as middle and so forth arise according to one's own nature; therefore, by the limitation of the knower's conception, they regard the earthly principle as the lowest.

rows.grounds: refers to the earthly principle in this context

items.question: What topic begins with the description of the earthly principle?
premises: The earthly principle is the innermost of all and covered by all envelopes.
The text now turns to that earthly principle.
Within it, the arrangement of worlds is described.
items.inference: The cosmological survey of worlds begins from the earthly principle as the innermost level.
items.plain_english: That principle, standing in the innermost interval of all and covered by all the envelopes, is the earthly principle; here, within that earthly principle, the arrangement of worlds is described.

rows.grounds: identifies the ruler and his group

items.question: Who rules the Kataha Rudras in the lower cosmology described here?
premises: The Kataha Rudras are devoted to desire.
Their ruler is Ananta.
He is depicted mounted on a vessel within the waters, reeling from drink.
items.inference: The lower cosmological order is personified through Ananta as ruler of the desire-bound Kataha Rudras.
items.plain_english: The ruler of the Kataha Rudras, who are devoted to desire, is Ananta; he is mounted on a vessel within the waters, reeling from drinking liquor.

items.question: What is the position and measure of Kalagni's world in this cosmology?
premises: Ananta meditates on Bhairava while surrounded by serpents.
Above that region is the world of Kalagni.
Kalagni's world is said to rise to a height of one crore yojanas.
items.inference: The text places Kalagni's world above Ananta's domain and specifies its vast vertical measure.
items.plain_english: Meditating on the god Bhairava and surrounded by serpents, he is associated with the world of Kalagni above, which rises to a height of one crore yojanas.

rows.grounds: explains why he does not look up
refers to Kalagni or the ruler in that region
gives the reason for his placement

items.question: Why does the fiery lord of that region not look upward despite pervading the universe?
premises: He fears reducing the worlds above to ashes.
Although he pervades the universe, his burning affects this earth.
His destructive fire explains his restricted gaze and placement.
items.inference: The cosmology limits the fiery lord's upward gaze because his pervasive burning power threatens the worlds above.
uncertainties: The subject 'sa' is contextually taken as the fiery lord of Kalagni's region.
items.plain_english: For fear of reducing the worlds to ashes, he does not look upward; and although he pervades the universe, because he burns this earth he is understood in that lower position.

rows.grounds: indicates prior placement in the account
describes the space above the flame

items.question: How is the fiery region measured in relation to the hells above and below it?
premises: The fiery lord is regarded as below the hells.
His flame extends ten crores in measure.
Above that flame there is an empty space of half that measure.
items.inference: The cosmology gives precise vertical measures for the fiery region beneath the hells.
items.plain_english: Because he was made clear earlier in relation to the hells, he is regarded as below them; the mighty one's flame extends ten crores, and above it there is an empty space of half that extent.
